slides.title: Name it once
slides.text: A procedure is a group of steps with a name. Define it once, then call it wherever you need it. In Robo Route you build it as a My Block.
slides.alt: The team's My Block Zigzag (n) heads the program, with its note: By the Robo Route team. It climbs the zigzag staircase on the board.

slides.title: One block, many jobs
slides.text: Rooms of different depths? Do not make three blocks. Make one block, Room, that takes a number called steps. Each call hands it its own number.
slides.alt: My Block Dash (n) repeats n moves, and the calls underneath feed it different numbers: call Dash (7), (6), (5), (4), (3).

slides.title: Three rooms, one block
slides.text: Inside Room is repeat steps times. Room(1) and Room(3) run the same block with different numbers. That slot is a parameter.
slides.alt: Room (steps) is defined once with steps inside it, then called three ways: call Room (1), call Room (3), call Room (2).

slides.title: Split into subgoals
slides.text: A big level is easier as small jobs: collect the gems, climb the stairs, cross to the goal. Make one procedure per subgoal, and the main program is just calls.
slides.alt: Three named My Blocks split the job: GetGems, Climb and Cross, each defined in the tray and called in turn below.

slides.title: Notes and credit
slides.text: Pin a note that tells the truth about each block. If a block came from someone else, keep the line that credits them.
slides.alt: Three My Blocks carry plain-language notes: Sweep picks up the gems, Drop drives down the side, Home drives to the goal.

words.means: a named group of steps you can call
a slot in a procedure that each call fills
the number a call puts in the slot, like the 3 in Room(3)

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Functions and finish 4 levels, including one where you make a block with a parameter.
slides.alt: The team's My Block Zigzag (n) heads the program, with its note: By the Robo Route team. It climbs the zigzag staircase on the board.
